title: A Widow’s Wedding Anniversary
author: Susan Block
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Max-Wed-Anni-
Collage-680x454.jpg)

Wedding collage by Max

It’s coming up on our 34th Wedding Anniversary! Well, not exactly. Sad to say,
my beloved [Max](https://drsusanblock.com/max-lobkowicz-filangieri) [passed
away](https://drsusanblock.com/rip-max) last year after a major
[stroke](https://drsusanblock.com/birthday-healing) that shattered his brain
(but not our marriage). So, though we  _would_ be married 34 years on April
12, 2026 _if_ [Max](https://www.counterpunch.org/2025/06/20/captain-max-an-
extraordinary-life/) were alive, we were actually only married [33
years](https://drsusanblock.com/33).

But they were the best 33 years of my life! The number 33 is called a “Master
Teacher,” the highest level of Scottish Freemasonry, and Jesus preached, died
and was [resurrected](https://drsusanblock.com/fdr-resurrection) all at age
33. Alas, but the number 34 is not so special; it’s a “transitional” numeral,
and unfortunately, Max has already
[transitioned](https://drsusanblock.com/rip-max) in the other direction, and I
am still in such deep [grief](https://drsusanblock.com/bottomless-grief), I’m
not even trying to transition out of it. So, 33 is a *better* number,
numerically speaking.

Still, it’s kind of static.

Am I crazy to keep counting? Is there a rule that says once one of you dies,
the other must stop adding up the anniversaries? Maybe it’s a little macabre,
or overly sentimental. But what  _else_ should a still-weeping widow do on the
[anniversary](https://drsusanblock.com/max-collage-wedding) of the happiest
day of her life?

**Once Upon a Time in Philly…**

Yes indeed, Brothers and Sisters, Lovers and Sinners – those of you who knew
[Max](https://www.dignitymemorial.com/obituaries/los-angeles-ca/maximillian-
lobkowicz-12396320) well and those who have only heard his legends… One sunny
Spring Sunday in Philadelphia on [April 12,
1992](http://www.drsusanblock.com/travel/travel3.htm), Max and I got married,
and 34 anniversaries later, one of us is gone, having died in the arms of the
other.

Well, that last part involves another touch of poetic license. At the very
end, Max was hooked up to too many tubes to be in the arms of anyone but the
ICU angels. However, we were holding hands, as we so often did, my little hand
in his big one, fingers intertwined with so much love… right before his very
last squeeze. Then suddenly, I felt him leave me, sailing off into a sea of
mysteries, as the life left his big strong hand and his entire body. The Code
Blue alarms were sounded, and all the doctors and nurses came running in to do
whatever they could, but no one and nothing could bring Capt’n Max back to
shore.

That was almost a year ago, a little over a month after our 33rd, and this is
our first wedding anniversary where we’re separated – not just by distance,
but by dimensions. Having lived a life of
[Eros](https://drsusanblock.com/resist-thanato-celebrate-eros2) together, we
were struck by
[Thanatos](https://archive.drsusanblock.com/editorial/Terror/terror22.htm)
(death) – and now we’re more apart than ever. So, all I can do is honor the
memory of My Beloved Capt’n Max, aka [Prince Maximillian Rudolph Leblovic
Lobkowicz di Filangieri](https://drsusanblock.com/max-lobkowicz-filangieri)
(11/8/1943 – 5/13/2025) as best I can.

In that spirit, my fellow Bonobovillagers and I put on an amazing
[memorial](https://drsusanblock.com/max-to-the-maximus) (soon to be released!)
flowing with eulogies, tears, laughs, music and memories. There, I declared
Max’s birthday, November 8th, to be [Free Speech
Day](https://drsusanblock.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Max-
FreeSpeechDay.jpg). Don’t forget to celebrate by exercising your [Free
Speech](https://drsusanblock.com/free-speech-woman), or supporting someone
else’s – even when you don’t agree with them – as Max always did.

**Widow 's Wedding Anniversary**

Thanks to the über-capitalist internet, there’s now a gem for every
anniversary (remember when it was silver for the 25th, gold for the 50th and
for anything else, you were on your own?). Fortunately, the 34th is the opal,
and I already have a radiant fire opal ring presented to me by our
[HBO](https://drsusanblock.com/hbo) producer [Dave
Bell](https://drsusanblock.com/fetplay#DaveBell)right in front of a beaming
[Capt’n Max](https://www.counterpunch.org/2025/06/20/captain-max-an-
extraordinary-life/) – a rather romantic way to seal a TV deal, but those were
the days…

So, I’ve got the opal, but what else? It certainly doesn’t feel right to throw
a big party, [Erika
Kirk](https://x.com/search?q=erika%20kirk&src=typed_query&f=top)-style (or is
that now [Druski](https://x.com/druski/status/2036953526811930846)-style?).
Honestly, though I abhor [Mrs. Charlie Kirk](https://drsusanblock.com/go-
bonobos-2026#ErikaKirk)’s politics, I can’t help but feel some empathy for a
fellow grieving widow as she navigates her strange widowhood through all the
parodies and conspiracies (unless the
[conspiracists](https://x.com/search?q=erikia%20kirk%20conspiracy%20theories&src=typed_query)
are right!).

My hazy plan for our 34th is to scatter some of Capt’n Max’s
[cremation](https://drsusanblock.com/cremating-max) ashes in the ocean that he
loved so much. Maybe I’ll feel Max in the wind, hear him sing with the
seagulls or hallucinate that My Beloved walks on the water towards me, arms
outstretched to embrace me with his big strong hands (both of which are
working in my [fantasy](https://drsusanblockinstitute.com/sexual-fantasies))…

Of course,  _the best-laid plans may not get you laid the way you planned_ …
But I don’t plan to get laid – probably ever again! My plan is just to
sprinkle some of My Beloved’s sandy and *transformative* ashes into the free
and salty waves of so many of his glorious journeys.

“The Goal is the Journey,” as Max used to say, and our journey continues – in
our hearts and [collages](https://drsusanblock.com/max-collage-family)…

** "Wedding Anni Wonderland"**

The images that make up [Max Collage #8](https://drsusanblock.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/04/Max-Wed-Anni-Collage.jpg) of the “My Beloved Max”
collection, “[Wedding Anniversary Wonderland](https://drsusanblock.com/max-
collage-wedding-anniversaries),” range from the traditional splendor of the
"white wedding" to our second anniversary with the bonobos at the zoo, our 3rd
in San Francisco, our 8th in Amsterdam, our 10th in Paris, our 12th at DTLA’s
Bonaventure, our 16th at the Farmer’s Daughter Hotel by West Hollywood’s
Farmers Marker, our 22nd at the Green Horse in Inglewood, our 31sttaking the
RV up the coast and our 33rd rushing from Kaiser Hollywood Hospital to the
South Pasadena Care Center in an ambulance. Some couples take a limo for their
anniversary; we took an ambulance.

Each anniversary was like a wonderful ride in our Disneyland of a marriage,
but our favorite [anniversaries](https://drsusanblock.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/04/Max-Wed-Anni-Collage.jpg) were the big bawdy
[bacchanals](https://drsusanblock.com/26th-wedding-anniversary) we put on in
the bosom of [Bonoboville](https://drsusanblock.com/bonoboville). Since there
were pretty much always American
[wars](http://www.drsusanblock.com/editorial/terror/terrorjournal.htm) being
waged somewhere, our anniversary bacchanals were – besides being
[kinky](https://drsusanblockinstitute.com/kink), funny and fun – all
vociferously [anti-war](https://drsusanblock.com/32nd-wedding-anniversary).

I’d wiggle into my wedding corset (the dress broke on our wedding night – like
the hymen I didn’t have) for these funky,
[fetish](https://drsusanblockinstitute.com/wp-
content/uploads/2015/06/wbiehs1541.pdf)y, Bohemian extravaganzas, and Max was
proud to fit into his tuxedo jacket, topped off with his “I love Dr. Suzy” hat
(just in case someone didn’t know). Consenting adult
[revelers](https://drsusanblockinstitute.com/group)gathered around, dancing,
singing, speaking at the [Speakeasy](https://drsusanblock.com/speakeasy),
making love (not war) and making fun of [hypocrites,
](https://drsusanblock.com/active-
radio-6)[spanking](https://drsusanblockinstitute.com/spanking) effigies of
[Trump](https://drsusanblock.com/tag/trump) (who still needs many spankings!)
and other war criminals in sexy, lefty  _Commedia Erotica_ performances,
celebrating the adventure of romance and the longevity of true love, the
[Bonobo Way](https://bonoboway.com/).

These bacchanals were expressions of what we called “communal ecstasy,”
inspired by the late great [Barbara
Ehrenreich](https://www.counterpunch.org/author/barbara-ehrenreich/)’s concept
of “[collective joy](https://drsusanblock.com/bonobo-spring#collectivejoy).”

Through the [Erotic Theater](https://drsusanblockinstitute.com/erotic-theater-
therapy) of the [Mind](https://drsusanblockinstitute.com/erotic-hypnosis) and
the theatrical anniversary gatherings of
[Bonoboville](https://drsusanblock.com/bonoboville), we lived our
[fantasies](https://drsusanblockinstitute.com/sexual-fantasies) to the
fullest, while keeping a [foot](https://drsusanblockinstitute.com/feet-a-love-
story)(well, maybe just a [toe](https://drsusanblockinstitute.com/foot-fetish-
therapy)) in reality.

**To Marriage, Bonobo-Style!**

Marriage is not for everybody, and I’m sure most conservative (and
hypocritical) marriage advocates would not approve of our sexy, lefty
“Marriage [Bonobo-Style](https://bonoboway.com/)” – but it was perfect for us.

So, [pop a cork](https://drsusanblockinstitute.com/orgasm) tonight (or
sometime soon) for [lawfully
wedded](http://www.drsusanblock.com/travel/travel3.htm) love, [long-term
lust](https://archive.drsusanblock.com/editorial/Perfect10.htm) and [pro-
bonobo](https://drsusanblockinstitute.com/bonobo-liberation-therapy) marriage.
[Go Bonobos](https://drsusanblock.com/go-bonobos-2026) (it's our best chance)!
Go forth and find romance. You might lose it, but you’ll never forget it.
